title: Private incremental upgrade catalog and policy engine
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Implement an incremental upgrade catalog + policy engine for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) that drives safe, multi-stage upgrades and schema-aware migrations. The system will encode compatible upgrade paths, policy rules for gated rollouts, and produce a dry-run/rollback rehearsal plan that operators can execute before hitting customer environments.
background: Historically we've relied on large monolithic migration runners and ad-hoc canary steps for Private upgrades. This has increased blast radius when post-upgrade regressions occur and makes multi-cluster rollouts slow and manual. Customers with stricter change-controls have asked for an auditable upgrade policy layer that can verify compatibility, produce rehearsals, and enforce per-tenant rollout constraints.
goals: 1) Maintain zero-downtime upgrades for control plane services where possible. 2) Provide a catalog of supported incremental version transitions and baked-in schema migration plans. 3) Expose a policy engine that encodes rollout gates (health, telemetry, manual approvals). 4) Provide automated dry-run rehearsals and deterministic rollback simulations.
non_goals: We will not build a new orchestration runtime to replace Kubernetes operators. We will not attempt to automatically transform customer data schemas across incompatible major-version boundaries in the MVP.
design_summary: The design has three core components: (A) Upgrade Catalog: a manifest repository mapping versions -> allowed next-versions with migration artifact references (helm charts, migration SQL scripts, transform adapters), semantic compatibility tags, and TTL for support windows. (B) Policy Engine: declarative rules for cohorts, health gates, telemetry thresholds, and KMS-signed approval steps. (C) Rehearsal Runner: a dry-run harness that executes migration steps in a sandbox (helm dry-run + schema validation + fake traffic replay) and produces a deterministic rollback plan with state snapshots. The engine will integrate with our existing Private control plane via the upgrade-agent shim and publish events to the Console for visibility.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP) - catalog ingestion, simple compatibility checks, and rehearsal for control-plane components only. Phase 2 - cohorted rollouts for tenant clusters with policy enforcement and automatic metrics gating. Phase 3 - broaden to on-prem stateful db migrations with transactional fencing and staged replays.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrade catalog supports at least 3 version transitions and references artifact URIs
Policy engine can block rollout when latency or error-rate thresholds are breached
Rehearsal runner can perform a dry-run for a typical control-plane upgrade and emit a rollback script
End-to-end test in CI that simulates a canary and triggers automatic rollback on failure
Audit logs for every decision are emitted to the customer audit stream and to S3 for internal audits

blockers: Need final decision on artifact signing format (rpm signatures vs. OCI manifest annotations)
On-prem access patterns for rehearsal runner (requires partner work to provide sandbox clusters)
Telemetry retention quotas in Console — rollout gating needs 7d of high-cardinality metrics, ops requires a cost plan
notes: We should aim to make manifests human-editable but machine-verified; include schema versioning in catalog entries.
Consider a lightweight simulator mode for customers to rehearse upgrades in their own environment with a signed manifest
Plan a cross-team audit with security before enabling automatic cohort rollouts
